blocks.text: Following on from the message below, we now have the complete file history and the USPTO assignment record for each family on the licensor's schedule, and each family's next official deadline is entered on our docket so that nothing in the portfolio lapses unnoticed while the license terms are being worked out. The reading itself starts with the chain of title, because the rest of the review assumes the licensor owns what it proposes to license.

To move from collecting the record to reading it, we need the following:
1. The signed inventor assignments, or the employment agreements relied on in their place, for any family where the recorded chain does not run from every named inventor to the licensor. We can request these from the licensor's counsel directly if you would rather not relay them.
2. An editable copy of the patent schedule attached to the draft license, so that we can mark it up family by family.
3. A product description or data sheet for what {{fact:f:E-2025-001.client}} intends to make or sell under the license, since that decides which claims we read against the product first.

Where the record shows a gap or an encumbrance, I will set out what the documents say and leave the question of what it means for the license to counsel, who will give you that view in writing once the record is complete.
